observations.subject: requested document identifier and authorization resource

observations.subject: download authorization
observations.claim: If request.user is present and has_perms_owner_aware(user, view_document, root_doc) is false, the helper returns HTTP 403. The helper allows an unowned root, a root owned by that user, or a root for which Guardian ObjectPermissionChecker reports the specified object permission. observations.subject: version selector
observations.claim: With an explicit version parameter, resolution parses it as an integer and accepts the candidate only when it is the root itself or has root_document_id equal to the authorized root id. observations.subject: returned download

Thus version selection changes which related document row supplies the file, while original/archive selection changes the representation of that selected row; neither changes the root document used by the explicit authorization check.

observations.subject: resolution failures and deployment limits

result.scope: Bounded, source-only review of Paperless document Download behavior at revision 126ec414a8b65158368653a2604ae58415e43103, including DRF authentication configuration, root-document owner-aware authorization, version-family resolution, and original/archive file selection. answers.explanation: The download path is conditionally allowed. DocumentViewSet declares IsAuthenticated and PaperlessObjectPermissions, and its explicit file helper resolves the URL pk to request_doc (including deleted rows), derives root_doc, and checks request.user for owner-aware view_document permission on that root. has_perms_owner_aware succeeds if the root is unowned, owned by the caller, or covered by a caller object grant; otherwise file_response returns HTTP 403. Because ownership and grants are unspecified, source alone cannot choose among those branches. After authorization, the code chooses file_doc: an explicit version is accepted only if it is the same root or a version whose root_document_id equals the authorized root; without an explicit version, a pk already naming a version remains that version, while a root pk resolves to the latest version, falling back to the root. The original query flag does not select a different authorization resource: original=true serves the selected file_doc's original representation; otherwise an archive is used only when that selected row has an archive version. Accordingly, selecting another valid version changes the document row whose file is served, but does not change the authorization resource, which remains the logical root. An unrelated version is rejected as not found before serving. Invalid version syntax is also not found; missing rows are not found. Storage and response delivery can still fail independently.

paths.explanation: If request.user is absent/unauthenticated, IsAuthenticated denies request dispatch before the action. If the authenticated caller is neither authorized by the root's unowned/owner branch nor by a direct/group object grant recognized by ObjectPermissionChecker, the explicit root check returns HTTP 403 and no file is served.

policy.text: A caller lacking authentication or view authorization on the logical root document must not receive any original or archive representation of that root or its versions.

paths.explanation: If the authenticated caller passes the owner-aware view_document check on root_doc, and no version parameter is supplied, a requested version pk serves that version; a requested root pk resolves to the latest related version or the root if none exists. The selected row's archive is preferred when present unless original=true; otherwise its original is used.

policy.text: A caller authorized to view the logical root may download an available representation of that root or a version belonging to it.

paths.explanation: If root authorization succeeds and version parses to the root id or to a document whose root_document_id equals that root id, that selected row supplies the returned file. This changes the file-bearing row but does not trigger authorization against the version row itself; authorization remains against root_doc.

policy.text: Version selection may reuse logical-root authorization only when the selected version is cryptographically or relationally constrained by source to the same document family.

paths.explanation: If version is malformed, missing, or names a document outside the authorized root family, resolution produces not-found behavior and serve_file is not reached.

policy.text: Selecting an unrelated or invalid version must not permit access to a file outside the authorized logical document family.

answers.explanation:
Source behavior is conditional because the caller's ownership and object grants are unspecified. DocumentViewSet declares IsAuthenticated and PaperlessObjectPermissions. DRF's IsAuthenticated requires a present authenticated request.user. For the file operation itself, file_response resolves the URL pk with Document.global_objects, obtaining request_doc and then root_doc. It performs the decisive explicit owner-aware view_document check against root_doc: access succeeds when the root is unowned, is owned by request.user, or ObjectPermissionChecker finds the requested object permission; otherwise the helper returns HTTP 403. Source alone therefore cannot determine whether this particular authenticated user is allowed.

After that root check, the selected file-bearing document may differ from the URL-addressed row. With an explicit version parameter, the value must parse as an integer and the candidate must either be the root itself or have root_document_id equal to that root's id; malformed, missing, or unrelated candidates produce not-found behavior. Without a version parameter, a URL pk that already identifies a version continues to use that version, whereas a root pk resolves to its latest version, falling back to the root. Selecting another valid version therefore changes file_doc—the row supplying the file—but does not change the resource checked for authorization: the explicit check remains on root_doc.

Representation selection occurs only after authorization and version resolution. original=true causes use_archive to be false, selecting the chosen file_doc's original representation. Otherwise, the archive representation is selected only when that file_doc reports has_archive_version; if it does not, the original is used. The original/archive flag does not select another authorization resource.

Relevant denial and failure branches are: unauthenticated dispatch is denied by IsAuthenticated; failure of the root owner/grant check returns 403; a missing requested pk/root, malformed version, missing version, or version outside the root family results in not-found behavior; and file/storage errors can occur later independently. Relevant allow branches are conditional on the root being unowned, owned by the authenticated caller, or covered by an effective direct/group object grant recognized by the configured permission backend.

Independent policy comparison: if the intended policy is that authorization attaches to the logical document family represented by the root, and any root-authorized caller may download any version belonging to that family, the visible source is aligned because version selection is constrained to that family before serving. If policy instead requires separate authorization per version row or separate permission for original versus archive representations, the visible source does not implement those distinct checks. The task does not supply which policy is intended, so policy conformance is undetermined rather than assumed.

Representation selection occurs only after authorization and version resolution. original=true causes use_archive to be false, selecting the chosen file_doc's original representation. Otherwise, the archive representation is selected only when that file_doc reports has_archive_version; if it does not, the original is used. The original/archive flag does not select another authorization resource.

Relevant denial and failure branches are: unauthenticated dispatch is denied by IsAuthenticated; failure of the root owner/grant check returns 403; a missing requested pk/root, malformed version, missing version, or version outside the root family results in not-found behavior; and file/storage errors can occur later independently. Relevant allow branches are conditional on the root being unowned, owned by the authenticated caller, or covered by an effective direct/group object grant recognized by the configured permission backend.

Independent policy comparison: if the intended policy is that authorization attaches to the logical document family represented by the root, and any root-authorized caller may download any version belonging to that family, the visible source is aligned because version selection is constrained to that family before serving. If policy instead requires separate authorization per version row or separate permission for original versus archive representations, the visible source does not implement those distinct checks. The task does not supply which policy is intended, so policy conformance is undetermined rather than assumed.
